title: Evidence Threshold Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: xAPI
Learning Analytics
Non-Evidence Thresholds
Data Quality
Instrumentation
description: A p5.js lab in which learners move the hover, misclick and glance thresholds and watch a scripted 60-second learner session gain or lose xAPI statements, with a cost table of likely noise kept and likely attention lost, so they can justify a choice of thresholds.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Hover, misclick and glance thresholds (HOVER_MS, MISCLICK_MS, GLANCE_MS)
learningObjectives: The learner will justify a choice of hover, misclick and glance thresholds by observing how each changes the number and kind of statements produced from a fixed, scripted session.
prerequisites: The three MicroSim verbs and the evidence classes (Chapter 16)
Non-evidence thresholds and their stated reasons (Chapter 16)

accessibility.notes: All inputs are native sliders, a checkbox and a button; emitted and filtered acts differ by label and strike-through as well as color

controls.label: Misclick threshold (ms)
controls.purpose: Minimum run that emits an experienced statement

controls.label: Glance threshold (ms)
controls.purpose: Minimum page visit recorded as page dwell

controls.label: Show statements that were filtered out

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration with a two-sided cost readout that supports a written justification
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Threshold sliders over a fixed timeline with live recomputation and hover explanations
keyQuestions: Which acts does each threshold remove, and which should it keep?
What does an over-strict threshold throw away?
Why does no threshold change the answered statement?
commonMisconceptions: A lower threshold always means better data
Thresholds remove bad learners rather than sub-threshold acts
The default values were fitted to learner data
assessmentOpportunities: Stating the safe band of hover thresholds for the session
A written justification naming the noise kept and the attention lost

simulation.model: Rule-based filter over a fixed scripted session of 16 acts
equations: hover emitted if duration >= hover threshold
run emits experienced if duration >= misclick threshold
page dwell emitted if duration >= glance threshold
assumptions: Session acts and durations are scripted and illustrative
Optional press statements for Start/Pause are not shown
